sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the header information for the maamar delivered on Shabbat Parshat Kedoshim, the second day of Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5736.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbat Parshat Kedoshim,
the second day of Rosh Chodesh Iyar, 5736*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the paradox of G-d having a throne and footstool, and resolves it by identifying heaven and earth with Torah and mitzvos, while the ultimate dwelling for Atzmus is through self-nullification.

translations.translation: "The heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool,
which is the house that you will build for Me... and to this one I will look: to the poor and broken-spirited..."1,
and the precise point in this is known2,
for He has no bodily form3
so how can it be said [He has] a throne and a footstool?
And also it must be understood what is meant by "which is the house that you will build for Me... and to this one I will look: to the poor and broken-spirited,"
what is the virtue of the poor and broken-spirited,
for although "which is the house that you will build for Me,"
nevertheless "to this one"
(to the poor and broken-spirited)
"I will look."
And the point of the explanation of this is,
that heaven and earth are Torah and mitzvos
(as explained at length in Torah Or4),
which in general is the service of Nefesh HaElokis and Nefesh HaBahamis5.
And "house" is the service of "with all your might"6
which is above limitation7,
coming from the aspect of Chayah and Yechidah5.
And the explanation of "which is the house that you will build for Me" is8,
that even the service that comes from the encompassing lights of Chayah and Yechidah,
through which the supernal encompassing lights are drawn down,
this is not "the house that you will build for Me"
("for Me" — for My Atzmus),
for even the most supreme encompassing lights are merely an illumination.
"To this one I will look: to the poor and broken-spirited"9,
for through self-nullification
(poor and broken-spirited)
there is a drawing down of Atzmus
("to this one I will look").

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the haftarah of "The heavens are My throne" to Shabbat Rosh Chodesh, explaining that the moon's nullification at its new moon allows it to receive a new light from above, paralleling the drawing down of Atzmus through self-nullification.

translations.translation: B)
And it can be said,
that this is also the connection and relevance of the haftarah "The heavens are My throne" to Shabbat Rosh Chodesh,
for on Rosh Chodesh is the birth of the moon,
when then
(at the time of the new moon)
it is only a point,
which indicates its self-nullification10,
that it has nothing of its own at all11.
And moreover,
that in the moment just before the new moon it is in complete nullification,
that it is not even like a point,
and specifically through this its new moon is brought about12.
And through its self-nullification,
it receives a new light from the sun,
for the source of the drawing down of this light is not from the sun itself
(for there is nothing new under the sun13)
but from above14
from the Sun15.
And this is that on Shabbat Rosh Chodesh we read the haftarah "The heavens are My throne... and to this one I will look: to the poor and broken-spirited...,"
for the drawing down that comes through self-nullification16
is a most exalted drawing down,
as explained above.
